review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–99) and did not open any other sources. The only repeated pattern is in the three `sorted_basis_*` lemmas. Each starts with `rw [basis_reindex_toMatrix, hf _ _ ...]`, and the reindex-to-matrix step is already factored into `basis_reindex_toMatrix`. After that, each lemma has a different short finish: `Matrix.one_apply` with `ite_eq_right`, `Matrix.one_apply_eq`, or `Matrix.one_apply` with `e.injective.eq_iff`. Each proof is one or two lines, and the lemmas use different hypotheses (`hm`, none, `hfirst`). A shared helper would be a thin wrapper and would not make the file clearer. Two other pairs have shared structure: `basis_reindex_equivFun` and `basis_reindex_toMatrix`, and `realDenominatorGrid_comp` and `basis_reindex_grid`. These are routine simp or funext unfoldings, and `basis_reindex_grid` already reuses the other two lemmas. I found no nontrivial reasoning repeated in two proofs. I did not check for duplication of Mathlib API, because the rubric does not cover it.
